content: To take this medication, mix at least one teaspoon (5 milliliters) of the medication with a beverage or soft food and consume it immediately. Suitable beverages include water, milk, apple juice, orange juice, cranberry juice, or carbonated drinks. Soft foods such as yogurt, applesauce, mashed banana, or porridge can also be used. If using tablets, crush them and mix thoroughly with a soft food like yogurt, applesauce, mashed banana, or porridge. Consume the entire mixture immediately. The 20-milligram tablets can also be administered through a feeding tube if necessary. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If prescribed daily, take it at the same time each day.g., Monday, Wednesday, and Friday) at the same time of day. Continue taking this medication, along with any other tuberculosis (TB) medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, joint pain, and headache. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Bedaquiline may cause a rash, which is usually not serious, but it can be difficult to distinguish from a rare rash that may indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before starting bedaquiline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Bedaquiline may affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), and the risk of this condition may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using diuretics (water pills) or experiencing severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Additionally, bedaquiline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of bedaquiline from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If using the 20-milligram tablets, keep the drying agent (desiccant) in the bottle. If using the 100-milligram tablets, they may be stored in another container for up to three months if necessary. Always tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. If you miss a daily dose during the first two weeks of treatment, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. If you miss a dose from week three onward, take it as soon as you remember, then return to your usual three-times-a-week dosing schedule. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., liver function, EKG, potassium, calcium, and magnesium levels) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. Keep all medical and lab appointments. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
